papers.what_it_is: A theory paper with small simulations proving that a single signal qubit repeatedly interacting with fresh copies of an arbitrary input state is a universal approximator of bounded continuous functions of that state (an existence result), with polynomial-fit, purity, entanglement-entropy and Bloch-sphere experiments.

assertions.value: The authors state that the circuit can approximate any bounded continuous function using only one ancilla qubit and single-qubit measurements, provided that sufficiently many copies of the input state and, in general, sufficiently many layers are available.
quotes: The circuit can approximate any bounded continuous function using only one ancilla qubit and single-qubit measurements, provided that sufficiently many copies of the input state and, in general, sufficiently many layers are available.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract's summary of Theorem 2; the theorem's own statement is entered separately.

assertions.value: The authors state that, by alternating entangling unitaries with mid-circuit resets of the input register, the architecture realizes a discrete cascade of completely positive and trace-preserving maps, analogous to collision models in open quantum system dynamics.
quotes: By alternating entangling unitaries with mid-circuit resets of the input register, the architecture realizes a discrete cascade of completely positive and trace-preserving maps, analogous to collision models in open quantum system dynamics.
assertions.certainty_reason: A theoretical statement the paper gives with little or no proof in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that, no matter how many qubits the input state contains, the model requires just one extra qubit (the signal register) to achieve universality.
quotes: In fact, no matter how many qubits the input state contains, the model requires just one extra qubit (the signal register) to achieve universality.
assertions.certainty_reason: A summary of Theorem 2, stated in the introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that the total number of qubits required by the model does not scale with the number of layers, since only the input register and one working qubit are needed.
quotes: As a result, the total number of qubits required by the model does not scale with the number of layers, since only the input register and one working qubit are needed.
assertions.certainty_reason: The introduction's statement of the qubit-reuse consequence; the number of copies does grow with the layers.
